correctness.rationale: For q>=4,r>=2, rooted congruent cycle bouquets have N=1+r(q-1). The nonstandard one-cycle lemma bounds sum(g-mean)^2<=b_q-a_q²/q (distance profile sharp) via the permutation-extreme cycle argument of Yancey Section 2.3; the objective is strictly convex and permutation invariant, justifying the adaptation from log-mgf to quadratic variance. With root set zero and S_i=sum petal values, global variance J=sum Q_i-(sum S_i)^2/N; separate strict convexity of the bounding quadratic on [-a_q,a_q]^r forces S_i=±a_q and balanced signs. This proves exact spread r*b_q/N -1_{r odd}a_q²/N² and ALL maximizers ±root distance on each petal. Exact a_q,b_q show even-to-odd decrease and odd-to-even increase. Independently enumerated rooted cycle Lipschitz-polytope extreme points q=4..7 and their bouquet combinations r=2..4, matching predicted variance and parity; finite tests only corroborate all-integer proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for the one-point sum of r congruent noncomplete cycles, optimizer rigidity and alternating variance law; the sharp one-cycle profile is prior in Yancey's permutation-extreme structural analysis, and clique bouquets with q=3 are excluded. Search of published related cactus, cycle, graph-spread items found no matching 1-sum formula. A general one-point graph gluing theorem may still imply it, so priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: Cycle centered variance lemma is adapted from Yancey’s structural exclusion for a different strictly convex symmetric functional; exact adaptation depends on using the documented permutation argument, not merely citing a logarithmic-mgf inequality as equal to variance.
An unindexed broader graph 1-sum/gluing spread theorem could dominate the exact bouquet formula.
Only congruent q>=4 simple unit cycles and uniform masses considered; no heterogeneous cactus classification.
